newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT says will decide on Leykam in 1997.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT says will decide on Leykam in 1997.

text.p: Dutch paper and packaging group KNP BT said on Wednesday it would decide this year on the future of its ailing paper unit KNP Leykam.
Board member Rob Bonnier said the company would try to find a partner for Leykam during the year, adding that a stand-alone situation could be envisaged if KNP BT could not find a partner for it.
"We are still talking. We are talking with several parties," he told a news conference.
Chairman Frank De Wit declined to identify possible parties interested in Leykam.
KNP BT said its paper unit was the main cause of the drop in the company's operating results in 1996.
"It's a structural problem, which needs structural measures," De Wit said, pointing to problems within the European paper sector as a whole.
KNP BT is in the middle of a 1.2 billion guilder investment programme in Leykam, intended to raise production and productivity.
"This is to increase capacity by 15 percent within three years," De Wit said.
He repeated that the reorganisation announced last month, cutting 1,000 of 4,600 jobs at KNP Leykam, would also lead to cost reductions of an annual 100 million guilders.

"The current situation (at Leykam) can be significantly improved by both cost reductions and an increase in productivity, but additionally, we hope to achieve further synergies through the cooperation with a partner," De Wit said.
He said a partnership might trigger more concentration moves in the European paper sector.
"We are talking with other (paper) companies, and so are others. I expect a considerable acceleration in the concentration process," he said.
KNP BT targets an operating profit as a percentage of average invested capital -a return on investment(ROI)- of above 15 percent. From 13.5 percent in 1995, ROI fell back to 9.4 percent in 1996.
In 1996, its distribution unit had a ROI of 17.1 percent, packaging achieved an ROI of 13.2 percent, while Leykam had a negative ROI.
